One Metro government

Since 1963 the city and Davidson County have run as a single Metro government, so valuation, billing and deed recording for a sale all sit under one roof. Only Belle Meade, Ridgetop and Goodlettsville levy a separate city tax. Hilly terrain around the Cumberland River means listings often mention slopes and retaining walls.

Mid-2025 estimates show 721,074 residents in Nashville-Davidson, up 4.6% from 2020. Owners occupy just 52.4% of homes, so landlords, heirs and people changing jobs make up a big share of sellers. The median owner-occupied value is $413,600 and median rent is $1,586. A downtown condo and an Antioch ranch house sit far apart, so use sales near your address to set a price.

The 2025 reappraisal and your tax rate

Values were mailed on April 18, 2025, and the median parcel rose 45%, with council district medians running from 38% to 54%. The state first trimmed the old rates to revenue-neutral levels, and then Metro raised them again. Owners in the Urban Services District pay $2.814 for each $100 assessed, and those in the General Services District pay $2.782. Those are jumps of 26% and 39% over the certified rates.

Only the value can be appealed. The Mayor and Metro Council set the rate. State law taxes a house on 25% of its appraised value. For the next cycle's informal review and appeal dates, call the Assessor's appraisal staff at 615-862-6059.

The Trustee's bill at closing

The Trustee prints one annual statement for the parcel's owner of record, covering the whole calendar year. Your title company should divide it on the settlement sheet, and a sale in November means you owe for the months you owned the house. Unpaid amounts follow the parcel, so confirm the year is settled before you hand over keys.

  • Statements go out in early October, and the first Monday of October is the due date.
  • Payment is interest-free through the end of February.
  • From March 1 the Trustee adds 1.5% per month.
  • A card payment adds 2.55% (minimum $2.00); an e-check adds $1.00.

Tennessee does not require the Trustee to mail a notice, so a lost bill does not pause interest. Parcels that stay delinquent go to a tax sale auction, with a one-year redemption right for the owner. To pay in person, go to Suite 220 of the Howard Office Building, 700 President Ronald Reagan Way, weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Mail goes to PO Box 196358, Nashville, TN 37219-6358.

Property tax relief

Owners 65 and up can apply for a freeze, and low-income elderly owners and disabled owners, including a disabled former service member, can claim relief. The Comptroller's 2026 table caps freeze income at $54,900 here. A veteran rated 100% disabled has no income test, and the relief applies to the first $175,000 of market value.

Tell the buyer's side early so the settlement figures reflect the real bill. The Trustee's office at 615-862-6330 can say which proofs of age, residence and income it wants.

Deeds at the Register of Deeds

The office at 300 Deaderick Street files deeds and accepts remote filings. The state adds 37 cents for every $100 of price on the transfer, and there is a $10 minimum on the recording fee. The office's online calculator gives exact totals. It takes original documents with notarized signatures, and staff cannot draft a deed or search for liens. Hire a title company or attorney for that.

Anyone can search the indexes in the office, and online access is sold by subscription. Ask the closer to record on the day you sign so the new deed is indexed quickly, and order a certified copy later if you want one for your files.

Short-term rental permits

A Nashville short-term rental permit does not transfer. Metro Codes ties it to a named holder and one address, bars assignment to another person, entity or address, and cancels it on any change of owner, including a move from a person into a trust or LLC. A new owner who wants nightly guests must apply from scratch.

  • A permit lapses 365 days after issue unless renewed.
  • The guest count tops out at twice the sleeping rooms plus four, never more than 12.
  • Renters must be 21 or older.
  • Three code violations can cost the holder the permit.

Put the permit status in your offer paperwork. The Metro Codes operating rules spell out every condition.

Older houses and what buyers ask

Housing from many eras sits side by side. Sellers of older houses can pull the year built and living area from the Assessor's record and check them against the listing. Roof age, foundation movement and old wiring are what buyers most often ask about, so price those in or fix them before showings. Families may also ask whether a house is zoned for a magnet school, and Metro Nashville Public Schools can answer that for a specific address.

Documents to gather before closing

  • Your latest Trustee statement and proof of what has been paid this year.
  • Your deed, so the legal description can be checked against the contract.
  • Your mortgage servicer's name, so the payoff letter can be ordered early.
  • Any short-term rental permit and its operating history, if guests have stayed.
  • Proof of any tax freeze or relief enrollment, such as age and income records.

Ask the closer to confirm who is recording the deed and on which day. A lien that turns up at the last minute can delay the closing, and Register of Deeds staff cannot search for liens for you.

Listing or selling for cash

A listing draws the biggest crowd of buyers, along with showings, appraisals and repair demands. Selling to a cash buyer who takes the house as it is gives up some of that reach for speed, since closing waits on title work and not on a lender.

Either way, get the price in writing, state in the contract who pays the recording tax and have a title company prepare and file the deed. Clear liens, back taxes and rental permit questions before closing day.

Frequently asked questions

Will I owe Davidson County tax if I sell in November?

Yes, for the months you owned the house. The bill covers the calendar year, and the settlement statement should split it between you and the buyer.

Can a Nashville owner contest the tax rate?

No. Only the value can be appealed, and the Mayor and Metro Council set the rate. The 2025 figures were $2.814 and $2.782 for the two service districts.

How much does it cost to record a Nashville deed?

The state transfer tax is 37 cents per $100 of price, and the recording fee has a $10 minimum. The Register of Deeds has an online calculator for exact totals.

Can a buyer take over my short-term rental permit?

No. Metro Codes bars assignment to another person, entity or address, and a change of ownership cancels the permit. The new owner must apply again.

Where can I pay Metro property tax in person?

At the Trustee's office, Suite 220 of the Howard Office Building, 700 President Ronald Reagan Way. Hours are weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Before you sell in Memphis

A Memphis sale runs through Shelby County offices as much as city hall. The county assessor values the property, the Board of Equalization hears value disputes and the Register of Deeds records the deed. Knowing who handles which step keeps a quick sale from stalling.

Memphis had 609,647 residents in mid-2025, about 3 percent fewer than in April 2020. The citywide median home value of $169,000 hides big swings from block to block, so judge your own price by your street and your house's condition.

Fewer than half of Memphis homes are owner-occupied, so rentals are a big slice of the market. If tenants live in your house, hand any buyer the lease terms and dates at the start.

How city and county tax bills work

Memphis mails its own bill, separate from the one Shelby County issues. The City Council sets the rate in June. Anything unpaid after August 31 is delinquent and gains 1.5 percent each month. Values come from the Shelby County Assessor's roll as of January 1.

Extra charges can ride along on the city bill: grass cutting, demolition and board-up, new sidewalk work and anti-neglect fees. A closing agent wants every line cleared, so ask the City Treasury at 125 North Main Street for a current statement before you list.

The county runs on a different calendar. County tax is payable the first Monday of October, interest-free through February 28, and delinquent March 1. Residential parcels are assessed at one quarter of appraised value.

Tax help for owners 65 and older

  • The Tax Relief and Tax Freeze programs are open to owners 65 or older, and both carry income limits that the state resets each year.
  • A Quarterly Payment Program lets owners 65 and up split the year into four equal payments, due August 31, November 30, February 28 and May 31.

Call the City Treasury at 901-522-1111 to apply, or to ask how selling the house would change your enrollment in any of these programs.

Selling with back taxes

Real estate taxes unpaid for a full year go to delinquent tax attorneys the following February 1, and attorney fees make the debt harder to clear. A sale resolves it: the closing agent pays the back taxes, plus any weed cutting or demolition charges on the bill, out of your proceeds.

Get written figures from the City Treasury and the county early, and do not wait for the attorney stage.

Appealing your assessment

The Shelby County Board of Equalization takes challenges during a spring window. For 2025 values it ran May 1 through June 30, 2026. A value left alone usually stands for the year, so phone the Board at (901) 222-7300 to learn when the next period opens.

Filing is free. The Board's online eFile site runs only during appeal season, hearing notices go out two or more weeks ahead, and you must bring every exhibit to the hearing. A hearing can lower the value, raise it or leave it alone.

A softer first step is the Assessor's informal review. It is not a formal appeal, though the office says it settles many disagreements. Useful backup includes closed sales of similar houses nearby, a recent private appraisal and dated photos showing condition. The Assessor's Action Center is at 901-222-7001.

Recording at the Shelby County Register of Deeds

Deeds are filed at the Register of Deeds on Mullins Station Road, Building W-3, in the 38134 area. The office says a recorded deed is typically mailed back within one business day, with a scanned image posted online. Holders of an e-file account can submit documents without visiting.

Recording triggers Tennessee's realty transfer tax: 37 cents for every $100 of the larger of sale price or fair value. The grantee, who receives the property, owes it, and must state the true consideration under oath on the instrument before the clerk accepts it.

Register's staff only record. They cannot give legal advice or help with wording, so use a closing attorney or title agent for the deed itself. The office will find an earlier deed or a trust deed release and certify a copy.

Short-term rental registration

A Memphis house used for short-term rentals must be on the Short-term Rental Registry run by the Memphis and Shelby County Division of Planning and Development. Operating a business also takes a City of Memphis license and a Shelby County license, $15 each. If the house you are selling hosts guests, tell the buyer which registration it holds and collect the paperwork.

Ask the Division for current fees and pending changes before listing, since the City Council has been working on enforcement language.

Documents to gather before you list

Pulling a few papers together early saves the closing agent a week of phone calls.

  • The latest city bill and a current statement from the City Treasury, with any grass cutting, demolition or board-up charges itemized.
  • The county bill, which follows its own October to February calendar.
  • Your earlier deed or any trust deed release, which the Register of Deeds can locate and certify.
  • Lease terms and dates if a tenant lives in the house.
  • Short-term rental registration papers, if guests ever stayed there.

Memphis sellers sometimes assume a quick sale means skipping this folder. It does not. Taxes, liens and the deed all still pass through the title agent, and having them ready is what makes a short closing possible.

What a cash sale skips

Storm wear and aging systems are the usual sticking points on older Memphis houses. A buyer with a mortgage may ask for a roof or air conditioning credit after the inspection. A cash buyer usually prices those items in and skips the negotiation.

  1. Share the property details and any lease with the buyer.
  2. Receive an offer, accept it and let the title agent open the file.
  3. Collect payoff figures from the City Treasury and the county.
  4. Sign the deed at closing, and the grantee's side records it in Shelby County.

With no lender involved, you and the buyer can pick a closing day that suits your move. Nobody is waiting on a bank appraisal or a loan committee, so the date holds unless the title search turns up a surprise.

Frequently asked questions

Who pays the transfer tax on a Memphis home sale?

The buyer, as the party taking title. The state charges 37 cents per $100 of the larger of price or value, collected at recording. Read your contract, since it may shift the cost.

When can I appeal my Memphis assessment?

The Board of Equalization took 2025 appeals from May 1 through June 30, 2026. Call (901) 222-7300 for the next window, and try the Assessor's informal review at 901-222-7001 in the meantime.

What if I owe back city taxes on my Memphis house?

Interest builds at 1.5 percent a month after August 31, and a full year unpaid sends the debt to attorneys on the next February 1. The closing agent pays back taxes and any cleanup charges from your proceeds.

How fast does Shelby County record a deed?

Typically about one business day. The office mails the deed back and posts an image online, and e-file account holders can send documents electronically.

Can Memphis owners over 65 get tax help?

Yes. The city offers Tax Relief, Tax Freeze and Quarterly Payment programs for owners 65 or older, and the first two have state income limits. Call the City Treasury at 901-522-1111.

Which selling route fits a Knoxville house

There are three ways out of a Knoxville house: hire an agent, sell without one, or take a cash buyer's offer for the home in its present condition. Repairs, timing and what a typical buyer would pay decide which one fits.

An estimated 202,021 people lived in the city on July 1, 2025, up 6.0% from 2020. Only 46.6% of housing is owner-occupied, and those homes have a 2020-2024 median value of $239,700. Many sellers are landlords or heirs with a second house.

Areas of Knoxville buyers search

Buyers sort the city into five areas, and each pulls a different kind of house.

  • Downtown and the Old City: mixed residential and commercial blocks around Gay Street, next to the University of Tennessee campus and Fort Sanders.
  • South Knoxville: across the river, with Vestal, Island Home Park and Colonial Hills, served by Chapman Highway and Alcoa Highway.
  • West Knoxville: Sequoyah Hills, Bearden, Cedar Bluff and the Kingston Pike corridor near West Town Mall and Turkey Creek.
  • East Knoxville: Parkridge, Burlington, Morningside and Five Points along Magnolia Avenue.
  • North Knoxville: Fountain City and Inskip-Norwood, with Broadway as the commercial spine.

Interstates 40 and 75 meet west of downtown, I-640 bypasses the north side, and I-140 (Pellissippi Parkway) links West Knoxville with McGhee Tyson Airport and Maryville. The average commute for Knoxville workers is 20.2 minutes.

Hills, creeks and inspection issues

Sharp's Ridge, Brown Mountain and Beaver Ridge give the city plenty of sloping lots, and First, Second and Third Creek run through older neighborhoods. A buyer's inspector will usually look first at drainage, crawl space moisture, roof age and cooling equipment. Sellers who want to avoid that work sometimes choose an as-is buyer.

City and Knox County tax bills

Two bills arrive for a house inside the city, one from the City of Knoxville and one from Knox County. Unpaid tax on either one travels with the property to the next owner. A seller's promise to pay does not change what the city can collect from the buyer.

Selling a former short-term rental

A sale is allowed and needs no city approval. Still, ask the Business Tax Office what happens to the permit when ownership changes. Knoxville has required a permit for any stay under 30 days since its ordinance took effect in January 2018.

  • Type 2 permits cover non-owner-occupied units in non-residential areas.
  • Applications and yearly renewals go through the Business Tax Office.
  • The city pays Host Compliance to match online listings against permits, and unpermitted owners can be cited.

A 24-hour complaint line (865-337-8275) is part of that program, which is another reason to settle permit status before you list.

Permits and records that can slow a closing

Missing or open building permits are what most often hold up a Knoxville deal. The Plans Review and Inspections portal handles them, with separate tracks for single-family and townhouse construction, mechanical, electrical and plumbing work, and home occupations.

The Knox County Property Assessor revisits each property every other year and tracks permit progress, so a remodel or addition can raise the appraised value. After adding a room, request a field review so the record matches the house. Expect a new owner's name to appear in the assessor's system roughly a week after filing, and note that the state requires a sales questionnaire at every transfer of title.

How a Knoxville deed is recorded

Take the signed deed to the Knox County Register of Deeds, Suite 225, City County Building, 400 Main Street. Most documents are recorded on the day they arrive. Signatures need a notary or two witnesses. No recording deadline exists, although waiting can create legal trouble.

State transfer tax comes to 37 cents per $100 of the sale price. The Register will record a deed but cannot draft one or advise you legally. A certified copy of a lost deed is $1.00 a page. Knox County also sends a free email alert when something is recorded under your name. For the fee on your own document, call 865-215-2330.

Tax help for older or disabled homeowners

Two Trustee programs help owners who live in their homes, and each requires a fresh application every year. Here are the 2026 figures.

  • Elderly or disabled homeowner relief: a state-funded credit of up to $85, with a combined 2025 income limit of $38,470.
  • Owners with a total service-connected disability, and their widows or widowers: up to $444, with no income cap.
  • Senior tax freeze: open at age 65 and over with combined income below $63,470, covering a single home and up to five acres.

The relief works as a credit against payment, not an exemption, so a bill still comes. If you sell partway through the year, ask the Trustee how the credit is handled before closing.

Preparing for a Knoxville closing

Collect the city bill, the county bill, a payoff letter and any permit papers. Then ask the title company to confirm whose names are on the deed. Heirs need someone with authority over the estate to sign. Ownership can change after a death without a new deed if the correct wording and a death certificate are recorded, so a title company or probate attorney can tell you what your situation requires.

Timing a Knoxville sale

A listing adds weeks for photos, showings, a buyer's inspection and a lender's appraisal, and the buyer's loan can fail late. Cash removes most of that. If you need to be out by a certain day, say so on the first call and ask each buyer how title work, the tax proration and recording will fit that date. Settle the older bills first, because the deed cannot move cleanly with an unpaid balance attached.

Do repairs have to be done before a Knoxville sale?

No. Repairs are up to you. A buyer taking the house as is builds the work into the price, while a listing invites inspection requests.

Who is responsible for unpaid Knoxville property tax after a sale?

The buyer inherits it. Overdue tax stays with the parcel whatever the contract says, so call the Revenue Office and clear old balances first.

How soon can a Knoxville sale close?

Title work and whether the buyer needs a loan set the pace. After closing, the Register of Deeds usually records documents the day they arrive.

Can heirs sell a house they inherited in Knoxville?

Yes, once whoever has authority over the estate is able to sign the deed. A title company or probate attorney can say what your case needs.

What are the Knox County recording costs?

Tennessee statute sets the recording fee, and the state transfer tax adds 37 cents on every $100 of price. Call the Register of Deeds at 865-215-2330 for the fee on your particular document.

Historic districts and neighborhoods

Public schools fall under Hamilton County Schools. Confirm the school zone for an address before you quote it to a buyer.

Buyers' inspectors check roof condition, tree cover and drainage, and a seller who fixed those items in advance gets a cleaner negotiation. Hilly lots bring their own checks, and you can prepare a short file for them:

  • Engineer letters on foundations built on sloped ground.
  • Driveway grade and access details for steep lots.

Keep that file ready so it can go out with the first offer.

A cash buyer will usually look at the same items but price them in rather than ask you to fix them. If the house has had water in the yard or basement, or damage from a storm, say so in writing early. Buyers trust a seller who explains the history, and the offer comes faster.

The county assessor runs a countywide reappraisal every two years, and the next is scheduled for 2027. Houses are assessed at 25 percent of value. Your own notice shows the exact amount you owe.

Paying Sullivan County taxes and getting relief

Taxes can be paid through the end of February. The main Trustee office is at 3411 Highway 126, Suite 104, Blountville (423-323-6464). A Bristol office runs on Thursdays and Fridays from October 1 through March 13 at the Ralph Harr Justice Center, 801 Anderson Street, Room 139, phone 423-354-7037.

The county also runs a payment plan that splits an expected bill into ten equal monthly payments beginning in March. For older, disabled and veteran homeowners, a state tax relief program exists. For 2025 taxes the income cap was $37,530 based on 2024 income, with an additional $85 rebate from the county for elderly and disabled participants.

  • Homeowners older than 65 can qualify if combined income, including a spouse or co-owner, is within the cap.
  • Disabled homeowners recognized by the Social Security Administration use the same income cap.
  • Permanently and totally disabled former service members, and their surviving spouses, qualify without that cap.

Ask the Trustee which year's limits apply before you file. Bring proof of age or disability and your income records to the Blountville or Bristol office, and ask about the payment plan if March is a tight month.

Is there a way to challenge a Sullivan County value?

Begin with the county assessor, 3411 Highway 126, Suite 103, Blountville, 423-323-6455. Still unconvinced after that talk? The next stop is the county equalization board. Keep in mind that this office only values property. Rate complaints, billing questions and payments go to other offices.

The local board normally hears a dispute before the state will. If you disagree with the ruling, you have until August 1 of the tax year or 45 days after the local notice, whichever comes later, to file with the state. The judge there decides on evidence, and sales of comparable houses carry the most weight.

While the challenge is pending, keep paying the undisputed part of the bill on time. Skipped payments can bring penalties or end the appeal.

Zoning and permits

For zoning questions on a particular lot, call the Department of Development Services before you plan a rental or an addition, since use rules differ by district. Council meetings are held at the Slater Community Center, 325 McDowell Street, and the city's legal notices page posts agendas ahead of time, along with hearings on budgets and tax rates.

Where the deed gets recorded

Bristol deeds are filed in Blountville with the Sullivan County Register of Deeds, 3411 Highway 126, Suite 101, phone 423-323-6420. The counter opens weekdays at 8 am and closes at 4:30 pm. Transfer tax owed to the state is 37 cents per $100 of price.

Your title company splits the year's property tax with the buyer on the settlement statement. Check names and parcel details on the deed before you leave the title office, since a complete, notarized deed records without delay.

  • Get a payoff letter from every lienholder ahead of closing.
  • Settle who signs when an estate or co-owners are involved.
  • Check the Trustee's record for unpaid prior-year taxes, which the title company will expect to see settled at closing.

Selling with taxes owed in Bristol

Back taxes will not stop a Bristol sale. Whatever is owed gets paid out of the money you receive when the sale closes, so nobody asks you for a separate check. Ask the Trustee for the exact figure before you settle on a date, because late interest grows until the bill is cleared.

Cash buyers often move quickest when the title is clean, and they accept the house with its repairs. Listing it usually takes longer, though it can pay more for a house in decent shape. Whichever you pick, set aside payoff letters, your newest tax notice and a list of every owner on the deed. Get the buyer's closing date and title company in writing, and rank offers by what lands in your account after taxes, payoffs and recording fees.

On closing day, each owner signs in front of a notary, the title company divides the year's tax on the settlement statement, and the paperwork travels to the Register in Blountville. Carry a photo ID and your keys, and request the recorded deed afterward.

How much is the Bristol, TN property tax rate?

City homeowners pay $1.87 plus the county's $1.6129, a total of $3.4829, for each hundred dollars of assessed value in tax year 2025. Rates change yearly, so confirm the current numbers with the Trustee.

When are Sullivan County property taxes due?

Payment runs through the end of February. The Blountville Trustee's office, 423-323-6464, can give you the interest schedule for late payments.

Can I sell a Bristol house with unpaid taxes?

Yes. Closing pays the balance out of your proceeds. Call the Sullivan County Trustee for the payoff figure first.

Where is the Bristol Tennessee Register of Deeds?

It sits at 3411 Highway 126, Suite 101, in Blountville, and the phone number is 423-323-6420. Weekday hours run from 8 am to 4:30 pm, except on designated holidays.

Is Bristol, Tennessee the same as Bristol, Virginia?

No. They are two cities with separate governments that share a border at State Street. A house on the Tennessee side uses Sullivan County offices, Tennessee law and Tennessee taxes.

Rain and snow add up to about 59.4 inches across roughly 128 days a year here, so inspectors tend to press on roofs, crawl spaces and drainage. School attendance zones are set by Bedford County School District, which can confirm any address a buyer asks about.

Farragut at a glance

The 2020 census counted 23,506 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 25,121, a gain of 6.9 percent. Of 8,992 housing units, 5.2 percent sat vacant, with a 1.5 percent vacancy rate among owner homes and 14.3 percent among rentals. Few owner homes sit empty, which is useful context when you weigh a sale.

Hills, drainage and rain

Farragut sits in hilly ground between Blackoak Ridge to the north and Fort Loudoun Lake on the Tennessee River to the south. Hills mean sloped lots, and sloped lots mean buyers and inspectors pay attention to drainage, retaining walls and foundations.

Annual precipitation is 47.86 inches. Nearly 48 inches of rain a year puts roofs, gutters and crawl spaces on every inspection list. A seller who has patched a leak or regraded a yard should keep the receipts for the buyer. Walk the property after a storm and write down where water collects, since an honest note about drainage reads better to a buyer than a surprise in the inspection report. Retaining walls and foundations on sloped lots deserve the same treatment, with any contractor invoices attached.

Farragut property tax

Farragut levies no municipal property tax. Residents pay the Knox County rate of $1.55 per $100 of assessed value, with homes assessed at 25 percent of market value and commercial property at 40 percent. Your actual bill is on the trustee's site. Knox County sales tax is 9.25 percent, or 5.25 percent on groceries.

The Knox County Property Assessor reappraises on a two-year schedule and mails a notice whenever an assessed value changes. If you disagree with a value, the County Board of Equalization hears appeals in June. After a deed is recorded, the assessor's system can take up to a week to show the new owner.

Kingston Pike runs through the middle of town and I-40/75 runs along its northern edge. A commuter lot at Campbell Station Road and Campbell Lakes Drive serves ride sharers. Gas comes from the Knoxville Utilities Board, electricity from the Lenoir City Utility Board, and fire protection is subscription-based through Rural Metro. A buyer who learns about the Rural Metro subscription early will not be surprised by it at closing. Record the deed promptly, even though no statutory time limit exists. Signatures need a notary or two witnesses, and documents are usually recorded the day they arrive. The realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of the purchase price, paid by the grantee when the deed is recorded.

The assessor will send a sales questionnaire after ownership changes, including a private sale or a transfer into a trust. Tell the trustee where to mail later bills, and ask the Knox County Trustee how any current-year balance is handled at closing.
